home.title: See beyond the pixel
home.intro: Tala X says what can honestly be said about a photo. First, where the file comes from: a camera original, or a copy reprocessed by a platform such as WhatsApp. Then: where and when it was taken, whether it was edited, and whether the time is possible at the place given, from the position of the sun.
home.feature.1: Camera original or copy reprocessed by a platform
home.feature.2: Recorded place, date, time and time zone
home.feature.3: Editing software recorded in the file
home.feature.4: Position of the sun at the place and time given

legend.title: How to read the report
legend.intro: Each check gets one of these four states, always with its explanation. There is no overall score and no percentage: it is up to you to judge, check by check.
state.to_check.meaning: An anomaly that may have a legitimate explanation.
state.suspicious.meaning: A contradiction that is hard to explain otherwise.
state.unverifiable.meaning: The information needed is missing from the file.
says.title: What Tala X says, and what it does not
says.1: Tala X certifies nothing. “Camera original” means that the file carries the marks of a camera, not that what it shows is true.
says.2: Every result is an indication with its explanation, to be read with your own judgement. Metadata can be forged by someone who knows how.
says.3: Tala X is designed against laundering by platforms and recycled images, not against expert forgers.

sky.help: Look at the photo and choose what it shows. Your choice runs the analysis of the same file again: it is sent again, analysed, then deleted, like the first time.
download.note: The server makes the report: the file is sent to it again, then deleted. Changing the language asks for the report again in the same way. The downloaded report opens without a network connection.
